clue.text: Hard-plated fish from foreign river rolling part of roe

indicators.note: something rolling turns over, so the word for part of the roe is read back to front

blocks.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
roe is a mass of fish eggs, so one egg is part of it

explanation.surface: A tough-scaled fish taken from an Italian river is caught while rolling about its spawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The pogge is the armed bullhead, a small fish whose body is covered in bony plates.

clue.text: Stone cold performer turned up leading road race? Context not requiring drivers (12, three words)

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the little word that follows is written backwards

blocks.note: a pit is the stone of a fruit
C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap
a hand is a worker, one who performs a task
taken as written
the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the Isle of Man motorcycle road race

explanation.surface: A cold, stony performer heads a road race, though the event needs no drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: The drivers are golf clubs, not motorists: pitch-and-putt is a short golf course played with irons and a putter only.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch-and-putt is miniature golf on short holes, so the long-hitting wooden club called a driver is never needed.

clue.text: Brownish-yellow piece of pseudochrysolite

blocks.note: the letters run consecutively inside this mineral name

explanation.surface: A yellowish-brown fragment of a false gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a yellowish-brown earth pigment, and ochry is the adjective for that colour.

clue.text: This size, OS, is not right for OU gels

blocks.note: taken as written
these two letters are the leftover that is taken away

explanation.definitionFit: Size is a gluey sealant brushed onto plaster or paper, so the two words name the same sticky stuff.

clue.text: Elderly female or male entering, keen competitor on the circuit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Elderly female or male' looks like a choice of sexes; the 'or' just links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Gammer is an old rustic word for an elderly woman, the counterpart of gaffer.

clue.text: Page in section of the Koran, as above

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second

blocks.note: a sura is a chapter of the Koran

explanation.surface: A page reference within a Koranic chapter, marked as above.
explanation.definitionFit: Supra is Latin used in texts to refer the reader to an earlier passage, meaning above.

clue.text: Surfing tyro got mermaid helplessly rolling about

taken as written, before losing AID

explanation.walkthrough: MERMAID loses AID, then GOT plus MERM is rearranged into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grommet is surfers' slang for a young beginner, a learner on the board.

clue.text: Government file making sense?

clue.text: Tympanist missing entry – rather odd

clue.text: Food store – see one denied pant for meal concealed

indicators.note: the word named after denied is refused its place and swapped out for another

blocks.note: the reader is told to think of one food store, a pantry
the part removed from the start
taken as written, the replacement letters

explanation.walkthrough: Take PANTRY, drop PANT, and put a disguised MEAL in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: An almery, or aumbry, is an old word for a cupboard or recess for storing provisions.

clue.text: Gentleman's society I included in endless snub

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for society

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Signior is an old anglicised form of the Italian signore, a title for a gentleman.

clue.text: Fruit pest, rare thing enveloping most of stem

clue.text: Child pockets crumpled bumph – it's suitable for seedling

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun

indicators.note: paper crumpled up is scrunched out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
one who pockets something holds it inside

clue.text: Pair of characters in oyster place changing places for sort of smoothie?

clue.text: One needing psychiatric help grieves having wings clipped

blocks.note: to lament is to grieve

clue.text: Publicity stunt? It stimulates artificially

clue.text: Mass entering bewildering system, on edge? They're misbegotten

clue.text: Rate 'stormy' vague in precise measurement of space

blocks.note: taken as written

clue.text: Pliers somehow gripping ring device assisting plane's descent

somehow means in some unspecified arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Pliers somehow clutching a ring form part of an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoiler is a hinged flap on a wing that disrupts lift, helping an aircraft lose height.

clue.text: Chairman presiding over room as alternative to senior steward

or introduces an alternative

clue.text: Nick bits of earlier recorded stuff? Could be Grub Street denizens

the initial letters of the three words

explanation.definitionFit: Scratchers are scribblers who scratch away with a pen, the poor hacks associated with Grub Street.

clue.text: A number as introduction for unaccompanied wind

blocks.note: solo means unaccompanied
taken as written
N stands for an indefinite number

explanation.definitionFit: The solano is a hot, dusty easterly wind in south-east Spain.

clue.text: Cocktail coming from vineyards cheers

blocks.note: a cru is a French vineyard of a recognised quality
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

clue.text: This dinghy a liner envelops, result of degenerative process

clue.text: Stop fumbling after cross comes back – I won't catch a thing!
